findings.title: Commit markers are checklist checkboxes, not plain lines
findings.description: Every `Commit:` line (Tasks 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29) is written as `- [ ] Commit: …`, i.e. a checkbox item. The convention requires `**Commit**:` markers as plain lines, never checkboxes. The substantive placement rule is satisfied — markers sit at tested points, with uncommitted implementation tasks (e.g. Task 3, 5, 8, 10, 16, 19, 21, 23, 25) picked up by the immediately following test task's commit — but the marker form itself should be normalized to a plain `**Commit**:` line.

findings.title: All success criteria are covered by tasks, with correct sequencing and test-with structure
findings.description: No gaps: every Functional, Technical and Integration criterion maps to at least one task (mapping above), the 400 fixture captures (Task 18) correctly precede the reader tests that consume them (Task 20), dependencies flow forward (Task 7's read helper is extracted before Task 10 reuses it; `_is_counted` is parameterized in Task 5 and wired in Task 7), and there are no circular dependencies or tasks that don't trace to a criterion. Task sizes are proportionate to the slice, and each has success criteria a junior implementer can verify.
